title: Divine Humility for Human Exaltation
english: In the fullness of the ages, God spoke to us through His Son, without any mediation by prophets or holy voices, but directly through the Only-Begotten, who became flesh for our sake.

Through the prophets, God multiplied visions and became like them in their hands, and He who speaks is present, announcing peace and good things as the feet of one bringing good news on the mountains.
And again, He who speaks is present, as the one who brings good news on the mountains, proclaiming peace and announcing good things.

He did not take on flesh merely to remain poor alongside us, having cast aside his own inherent and divine riches; rather, it was so that we, who languish in want of heavenly gifts, might be made rich through his poverty.
And his name is called Angel of Great Counsel.
Though he is by nature the Son and co-heir with the Father, he submitted to birth from the holy Virgin and endured the conditions of human life for our sake.
As one being led toward the origin of sonship, he declared through David: 'The Lord said to me, You are my Son, today I have begotten you' (Psalm 2:7).
This 'today' points to the present time in which he became flesh, thereby making the declaration effective.
He exists by nature as Lord over all creation.

John bore witness to him, saying, 'He came to his own,' referring to the world as his domain, yet proclaiming an unfamiliar glory of the kingdom when he said, 'But I have been appointed king by him'—clearly indicating kingship under God the Father (John 1:11).

He endured these things so that, as a man made a son while remaining by nature God, he might forge a path through himself whereby human nature could share in sonship, and summon to the heavenly kingdom those who groan under sin’s tyranny.

Just as a hereditary burden—like an inheritance passed from father to all his descendants—comes to us from Adam’s transgression, weighed down with labor and mortality, so too does this divine provision extend to the entirety of the human race…

For in the fullness of the ages, He Himself spoke to us through Himself, the Son, without a prophet mediating anymore and without the holy voice, but through Himself having become for us the Only-Begotten, He made the words toward us.

We say that the Father speaks in the Son, not as through some particular human thing by means of something placed in between and carrying through to us not private words but rather the words from another, but in a particular voice, the one through the body speaking to us of the Son; for it was His, the Only-Begotten’s, flesh, and not another’s; for God being by nature became human while remaining God; then He made known to us the unutterable counsel of God and the Father; therefore it is called, 'And His name is called Angel of Great Counsel.'

Therefore rightly Paul speaks at the end of the days, having spoken in the Son to us God and Father; for He knew Him to be God, Emmanuel, having become also in humanity with us the God from Logos, He perceived the free 365 in the form of the servant, He confessed the fullness of Himself having emptied Himself for us, He beheld the height of the glory of Him who humbled Himself for us into lowliness, whoever also because of this cause is said to be appointed heir of all things, and yet ruling over all things as it is conceived and as it is God; again He returns into His own riches and after flesh; for He has not remained at all in our poverty.

title: Christ as the Divine Heir Who Enriches Creation
english: The divine attributes run through Christ splendidly. He receives these gifts not for himself but for us, for the Only-begotten, who is full and possesses the very nature of God, lacks nothing, yet enriches the entire creation with the blessings from above. Thus, in the economy of salvation, he has been appointed heir of all things as a man, so that he may recover as his own rightful inheritance those upon the earth who have been lawlessly plundered by the devil and the evil powers allied with him. God the Father said to him, 'Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance.' Having brought this request to its completion, he speaks to his own Father concerning us: 'Those whom you gave me from the world were yours, and they were mine; you gave them to me.' Therefore, let us consider how he advances into his existing wealth according to nature, both with and without flesh. For if those in the world belonged to the Father, how would they be perceived by the co-reigning Word with him? For he also said, 'All that is mine is yours, and all that is yours is mine,' and 'I have been glorified in them.' How then can he be commanded to ask? Yet he indeed receives the nations as inheritance and takes possession of the ends of the earth. Having cast off humanity's slavery under God, wishing to save them, the Maker of all things and Father sent forth into this world the Only-begotten God, the Word, so that having become flesh and conversed with men as a man, he might proclaim release to captives, sight to the blind, and announce the acceptable year of the Lord. Even if it were said that he takes and is appointed heir because of his humanity, we would not ignore the economy.

He receives these gifts not for himself but for us, for the Only-begotten, who is full and possesses the very nature of God, lacks nothing, yet enriches the entire creation with the blessings from above.

For how could he have become poor at all, unless it was by becoming among us—that is, a man who remains with God? The divine Paul urges us to think this way, and he necessarily adds that it is through him that God also made the ages. How then could this also be true? If indeed, in the last times of the age, the holy virgin bore to us Emmanuel, how can he say that through him the ages were made? And this is most rightly said.

For the Word from God the Father, who was begotten before every age and time, is declared to have become fleshly from a woman at the end of these days. He will in no way diminish the ancient dignity that belongs to God by possessing this nature—neither the newer aspect of the economy nor the eldest aspect of his existence will lose its own glory. For it is written: 'Jesus Christ yesterday and today the same and into the ages.' And that he, having appeared in flesh, bore witness to himself as the eldest in divine nature, will be confirmed when he says to the Jews: 'Truly, truly I say to you, before Abraham was, I am.' And the divine John the Evangelist also declared: 'He who comes after me has become before me, because he was before me.' For he is rich in all things, and Christ holds the first place.
Who is the radiance of glory. Just as the Father is unchanging, always remaining as he is.

title: The Eternal Word and Divine Substance
english: It is clear that the Father is not the Son, and so the Son dwells in what is his own, always remaining and never being turned toward the Father, in order that this character might be seen as truly belonging to the substance of the Father.
One might behold in him the surpassing excellence and glorious beauty that befit the one who begot him.
For he is true God from true God, light from light, life from life.
Yet he has surpassed the entire creation by as much as the Father himself can conceive.
He is unbegotten from one who is unbegotten, and not counted among those who are brought into being from non-existence.
For the Word was in the beginning, and the Word was God.

How then could it be true to say of him, 'He was not,' as those who wage war against the divine writings claim? For if they regard him as begotten, he must necessarily be made subject to all other things and accept the yoke of slavery, yet in no way does this apply to any of his own occurrences.
Therefore God is more rightly understood as proceeding from God.
For he upholds all things by the word of his power.
He has indeed become 'through him all things came to be, and without him not even one thing came to be,' yet he himself sustains all things toward an unshakable endurance.
We previously said that among the ancients, God established his will through Moses and the prophets.

But we have become, according to the prophet's voice, 'those taught by God,' for we have accepted him as our teacher—the Word from God who became incarnate for our sake, the maker of all ages, the radiance of the Father's glory, the very imprint of his substance.
Having observed these things from time to time, we will now add what follows.
These things are.....

The Word, who is God the Father’s Almighty, spoke and all things came into being; He commanded and they were created. He established them firm for the age and for the age of ages, issuing a decree that shall not pass away. For the nature of things brought into being does not possess incorruption, nor can it always remain as it is.

This is peculiar to the substance of the Highest over all. He upholds all things by the utterance of His own power. He indeed is subsistent Word, begotten from God the Father according to nature, while His utterance is all-powerful and active, easily accomplishing all things in strength.

Moreover, having made purification of sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty in the heights, having become so much better than the angels, as He has inherited a name more excellent than theirs. He shows the character of the Father’s substance and is the radiance of His glory, necessarily proceeding into the economy of the incarnation, through which we have been saved, enriched with the forgiveness of sins, and sanctified through His blood.
As He Himself says, the most wise Paul: 'In whom we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins.'
